messages:
ops-runner: Alert - spike in SRV lookup failures for service 'model-router' in us-east-2b. ~1.2k errors in last 2m, increased 5xx on downstream fleet. Rolling error rate across multiple clusters. Paging oncall.
incident-bot: SEV 2 Pager -> @maya (oncall). Incident ID: INC-1995004321. Auto-run diagnostics started.
maya: I’m on it. thanks. hitting the diagnostics now — checking CoreDNS pods + consul leader status in us-east-2b.
maya: quick summary: curl to internal discovery returns truncated SRV sets intermittently. Some nodes return empty records.
devon: @maya any signs of network partition between control plane and consul servers? last peering changes were 20m ago.
maya: checking VPC peering routes now. tailing CoreDNS logs — seeing a lot of: "servfail" and "proxy: upstream timed out"
zara: seeing similar egress timeouts in az metrics — egress NAT gateway in us-east-2b had a surge, but not full outage.
maya: Consul shows leader election noise, one server in us-east-2b is flapping to follower repeatedly. svc-health indexes show inconsistent service keys.
devon: ok that matches SRV inconsistency. If Consul leader is unstable, service discovery can return partial shards. Any recent config push?
maya: no config pushes in last hour per gitops audit. Likely infra-level: consul raft heartbeats delayed. grabbing raft metrics.
oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: @maya you’re primary, @devon is secondary. If escalate, page SRE Lead.
sre_lead: On call rotation, standing by. If consul raft leader continues to step down, consider draining CoreDNS replicas in that AZ and re-registering a stable consul member.
maya: trying a quick mitigation: cordon + restart CoreDNS pods only in us-east-2b to force fresh queries to other healthy consul nodes. Will do one at a time.
maya: command: ```kubectl -n infra cordon node-azb-12 && kubectl -n infra delete pod coredns-azb-0``` Doing rolling restart now.
zara: also enabling temporary routing to proxy SRV lookups via us-east-2a by updating internal-lb route table for model-router discovery if restarts don’t stabilize.
ops-runner: customer-impact: a few downstream customers reported transient 500s for model dispatch. No full outage but increased tail latency and errors for high-concurrency tenants.
devon: good call on cross-AZ proxy. We should also bump consul RPC timeouts to avoid rapid leader churn — small change, but if leader flaps repeatedly it could help.
maya: CoreDNS restart seems to have reduced local servfail counts by ~60% in the first 90s. SRV lookup success rates trending up.
incident-bot: Diagnostic report attached: consul raft leader term churn = 4 in last 5m; high RPC latency spikes at ~800ms.
zara: re: NAT gateway — cloud provider shows short route table recalculation during maintenance window 12m ago affecting SNAT pools intermittently.
sre_lead: If provider maintenance caused transient SNAT exhaustion, that would explain intermittent upstream timeouts. For immediate mitigation keep the rolling restarts and enable AZ failover routes.
maya: I started route update to add fallback path to us-east-2a for discovery: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-xyz --destination-cidr-block 10.0.0.0/8 --instance-id i-proxy-a` (dry-run first). Doing controlled update now.
devon: If route update goes well, monitor token caches. Also schedule a short consul server restart in us-east-2b once traffic reroutes — coordinate with SRE Lead.
ops-runner: Noting customer comms: support channels notified and we posted a status note: "Partial discovery degradation in us-east-2b; failover in progress."
maya: route update succeeded. SRV failure rate back down to baseline in 2 minutes, no new alerts. NAT metrics show normalized SNAT pool usage.
zara: consul leader is stable now, raft term unchanged for 3m. Candidate servers no longer stepping down.
sre_lead: Good. Keep the mitigation for 15 more mins and then slowly undo ephemeral routing. We'll follow up with post-incident notes and required RCA.
maya: I'm handing off to @devon for watchdog + postmortem steps. I'll add logs and timings to the incident ticket.
oncall-bot: Handoff: @maya -> @devon (15:37 UTC). Please acknowledge.
devon: acknowledged. collecting logs, creating postmortem draft. tentative cause: cloud provider SNAT/peering recalculation during maintenance causing RPC latency to Consul servers, triggering raft churn and SRV lookup inconsistencies. mitigation: rolling CoreDNS restarts + temporary route failover + restore SNAT capacity by provider ticket if needed.
incident-bot: Incident INC-1995004321 set to 'monitoring'. If errors spike again, page SRE Lead.
maya: thanks team. closing the active paging for now. :thumbsup:
